definition_zh: 清晰的；明亮的；晴朗的；畅通的；清楚； cleared；澄澈
definition_en: easy to see, hear or understand; free from clouds or blocks; to remove things from a place
core_image: 擦净的玻璃后一览无余的风景
scene: 雨过天晴，操场上空的云都被风吹走了。 The sky is clear after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 clear 是「晴朗的；明净的」（第 3 个义项：无云无遮挡）；句意是雨后天空晴朗。

derivatives.zh: 由 clear 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「清晰地；显然」
同源拉丁词派生，义为「清晰；清楚」
同源拉丁词派生，义为「澄清；阐明」

senses.title: Easy to see, hear or understand
senses.definition: easy to notice, hear or understand
senses.definitionCN: 容易被看到、听到或理解的
senses.example: Her voice was clear across the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音在大厅里听得很清楚。
senses.why: Nothing blocks the signal, so it arrives whole.
senses.whyCN: 毫无遮挡地抵达，信号完整呈现。

senses.title: Free from dirt or objects
senses.definition: transparent, or not blocked by things
senses.definitionCN: 透明或没有东西阻挡
senses.example: The water of the lake is clear.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水清澈见底。
senses.why: Dirt gone means the way through is open.
senses.whyCN: 污垢消失意味着通道畅通。

senses.title: Without clouds; bright
senses.definition: free from clouds or mist
senses.definitionCN: 没有云雾、天气明好
senses.example: The sky is clear after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后天空晴朗。
senses.why: An empty sky shows the same openness as clear glass.
senses.whyCN: 空无一物的天空与明净的玻璃一样通透。

senses.title: To remove people or things from a place
senses.definition: to make a place empty by removing what fills it
senses.definitionCN: 移走占位的东西使场所变空
senses.example: We must clear the desks before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前必须清理课桌。
senses.why: Removing what blocks makes the place 'unblocked'.
senses.whyCN: 移除阻碍之物，场所便「畅通」了。

senses.title: To become better; to pass
senses.definition: to improve or become free, as weather or debt
senses.definitionCN: 天气转好、债务结清等
senses.example: The sky cleared before our match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛开始前天空放晴了。
senses.why: A blocked state returning to its open form.
senses.whyCN: 受阻状态回到畅通的本相。

intro.en: Clear came from Latin clarus through French, bringing light and fame.
intro.cn: clear 经法语来自拉丁语 clarus，带来光亮与名声之义。

items.en: Latin clarus meant bright, clear and also famous.
items.cn: 拉丁语 clarus 义为明亮、清晰，也指有名。

items.en: Old French softened it into cler, meaning light and evident.
items.cn: 古法语演变为 cler，指明亮、显然。

items.en: Middle English took it as clere around the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 约十三世纪中古英语借入为 clere。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling as clear.
items.cn: 现代英语定型拼写为 clear。

items.en: The verb senses about removing blocks grew later.
items.cn: 关于清除阻碍的动词义是后来发展的。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alikes; the second gathers clarity words.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收清晰类词。

entries.definition: Free from dirt.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「干净的」，拼写与 clear 相近。

entries.definition: In a clear way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「清晰地」，是 clear 加 -ly。

entries.definition: Quick to learn.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「聪明的」，词首与 clear 相同。

entries.definition: Easy to see or notice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显的」，与 clear 的易懂义相近。

entries.definition: Allowing light through.
Containing nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「空的」，与 clear 的畅通义相关。

normalIntro.en: Remember clear by its Latin light root.
normalIntro.cn: 通过拉丁语「光亮」词根记忆 clear。

normal.en: clarus means bright in Latin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 clarus 表示明亮。

normal.en: clarify and clarity share this root.
normal.cn: clarify 和 clarity 共享这一词根。

normal.en: clear up can mean the sky improving.
normal.cn: clear up 可指天空放晴。

normal.en: make it clear means explain plainly.
normal.cn: make it clear 指把话说清楚。

normal.en: clear the table is an after-dinner job.
normal.cn: 饭后要 clear the table（收拾桌子）。

abstract.en: See every leaf sharp through washed glass.
abstract.cn: 想象透过洗净玻璃看清每片叶子。

abstract.en: Hear one voice standing out of all noise.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见一个声音从喧闹中脱颖而出。

abstract.en: Feel the wide sky with not one cloud left.
abstract.cn: 感受一片云都不剩的开阔天空。

examples.en: Please speak in a clear voice.
examples.cn: 请用清晰的声音说话。

examples.en: We cleared the leaves from the path.
examples.cn: 我们清除了小路上的落叶。

examples.en: It is clear that practice makes us better.
examples.cn: 显然，练习让我们进步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克利亚」——克利亚擦完玻璃，看什么都清晰。

root: 拉丁语 clarus（明亮的；清晰的；著名的）→ 古法语 cler → 中古英语 clere → 现代英语 clear；同根词有 clarity（清晰）、clarify（澄清）、declare（宣布，本义「阐明」）。

sensesIntro.en: Clear runs from unblocked seeing to open skies, open roads and clearing acts.
sensesIntro.cn: clear 从无阻的视线延伸到晴空、畅路和清除动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: nothing stands between you and the view
core.cn: 核心意象：你和景色之间毫无遮挡

branches.en: Easy to see or understand
branches.cn: 易看易懂的

branches.en: Transparent and unblocked
branches.cn: 透明畅通的

branches.en: A sky without clouds
branches.cn: 无云的天空

branches.en: Emptying a place
branches.cn: 清空一个场所

branches.en: Weather turning fine
branches.cn: 天气转晴

intro.en: The root clar- powers a bright word family.
intro.cn: 词根 clar- 支撑着「光亮」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin clarus lives on in several English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 clarus 保留在多个英语词中。

definition_zh: 自由；自主；自由权；不受……约束的状态
definition_en: the state of being free; the right to act, speak, or think as one wants
core_image: 打开的鸟笼：翅膀终于属于天空
scene: 毕业典礼上，校长寄语毕业生学会为自己的选择负责。 Freedom comes with responsibility.
sceneCN: 这里 freedom 是「自由（须承担责任）」的意思（第 1 个义项：自主的状态）；校长提醒学生自由与责任同行。

derivatives.zh: freedom 的词根形容词，义为「自由的；免费的」
free 加 -ly，义为「自由地」
复合形容词，义为「热爱自由的」

senses.title: The state of being free
senses.definition: the condition of not being imprisoned, controlled, or restricted
senses.definitionCN: 不被关押、不受控制、不受限制的状态。
senses.example: The animals enjoy freedom in the wide reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 动物们在广袤的保护区内自由生活。
senses.why: The suffix -dom turns the adjective free into the state of being free.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -dom 把形容词 free 变成「处于自由」的状态名词。

senses.title: The right to do something
senses.definition: the legal or moral right to act, speak, or think in a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式行动、发言或思考的法律或道义权利。
senses.example: Freedom of speech is written in the constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 言论自由写进了宪法。
senses.why: The state of freedom becomes a protected right.
senses.whyCN: 自由的状态被制度保护为权利。

senses.title: Not being affected by something unwanted
senses.definition: the state of not being affected by something unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 不受不愉快事物影响的状态。
senses.example: The village enjoys freedom from traffic noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄没有交通噪音的困扰。
senses.why: Freedom from a thing means the thing is kept out.
senses.whyCN: freedom from 某物，即该物被挡在外面。

intro.en: Freedom is a native build: free plus the state suffix -dom.
intro.cn: freedom 是本土构词：free 加状态后缀 -dom。

items.en: Freodoms roots are freo (free) and the suffix -dom.
items.cn: freedom 的根基是古英语 freo（自由）与后缀 -dom。

items.en: -dom meant judgment, state, or domain, as in kingdom.
items.cn: -dom 意为裁决、状态、领域，见于 kingdom。

items.en: Freodom first meant the state of being a free person.
items.cn: freodom 最初指「作为自由人的身份状态」。

items.en: The word widened to rights and liberties in law and religion.
items.cn: 该词在法律与宗教语境扩展到权利与自由。

items.en: Fixed phrases like freedom of speech became pillars of public language.
items.cn: freedom of speech 等固定搭配成为公共语言支柱。

note.en: Words shaped like freedom and words about rights and release.
note.cn: 与 freedom 形近的词及关于权利、释放的词。

entries.definition: very cold; different root from freedom
entries.definitionCN: 极冷的；与 freedom 无词源关系，仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: a state ruled by a king; shares the -dom suffix
entries.definitionCN: 王国；与 freedom 共享 -dom 后缀。

entries.definition: the state of being bored; another -dom state noun
entries.definitionCN: 无聊；又一个 -dom 状态名词。

entries.definition: freedom from control, often legal
not depending on others
self-rule of a person or region
entries.definitionCN: 自治；自主权；学术与政治用语。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the -dom state suffix and freedom's public uses.
normalIntro.cn: 围绕 -dom 状态后缀与 freedom 公共用法的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Break freedom into free + dom: the state of being free.
normal.cn: 拆分 free + dom：处于自由的状态。

normal.en: Compare the -dom family: freedom, kingdom, boredom.
normal.cn: 对比 -dom 词族：freedom、kingdom、boredom。

normal.en: Learn the big three rights: freedom of speech, choice, movement.
normal.cn: 记三大自由：言论、选择、行动。

normal.en: Freedom from fear keeps the bad thing outside the door.
normal.cn: freedom from fear 是把恐惧挡在门外。

normal.en: Freedom comes with responsibility: the gate opens both ways.
normal.cn: 自由伴随责任：门是双向的。

abstract.en: Picture an open birdcage against a wide sky.
abstract.cn: 想象辽阔天空下敞开的鸟笼。

abstract.en: Picture a document signing away old restrictions.
abstract.cn: 想象一份解除旧限制的文书。

abstract.en: Picture a hilltop where the whole valley is visible.
abstract.cn: 想象能望见整片山谷的山顶。

examples.en: The refugees finally found freedom in a new country.
examples.cn: 难民们终于在新的国家获得了自由。

examples.en: With a bicycle comes the freedom to explore the whole town.
examples.cn: 有了自行车，就拥有了探索全城的自由。

examples.en: The report calls for freedom from hunger for every child.
examples.cn: 报告呼吁让每个孩子免于饥饿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福瑞等」——福气瑞气等在门外等你走出来：freedom 就是门外的自由在等你。

root: freedom 为古英语本土复合词：freo（自由，词根 *frijaz「亲爱的」）+ -dom（状态、领域后缀，见 kingdom）。字面即「自由之状态域」；与 free、friend 构成同根家族。

sensesIntro.en: Freedom names the state of being free, the rights that protect it, and immunity from harm.
sensesIntro.cn: freedom 命名自由的状态、保护它的权利，以及免受伤害的安定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the open sky beyond the cage door
core.cn: 核心意象：笼门之外的整片天空

branches.en: Living without control or prison
branches.cn: 不受控制、不被关押地生活

branches.en: Speech and choice protected by law
branches.cn: 受法律保护的言论与选择权

branches.en: Rights enjoyed together by citizens
branches.cn: 公民共同享有的自由权

branches.en: Keeping fear, noise, or hunger outside
branches.cn: 把恐惧、噪音、饥饿挡在门外

branches.en: Freedom is both open gates and solid walls
branches.cn: 自由既是敞开的门，也是结实的墙

intro.en: Freedom is built with the state suffix -dom on the adjective free.
intro.cn: freedom 用状态后缀 -dom 附加在形容词 free 上构成。

latinIntro.en: The build is native Germanic; Latin liberty is the parallel borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 构词属本土日耳曼；拉丁借词 liberty 是它的平行对应。

definition_zh: 咔哒声；（鼠标）点击；发出咔哒声；一下子合拍
definition_en: a short sharp sound; to press a mouse button; to get on well suddenly
core_image: 开关按下的那一声轻脆的「咔哒」
scene: 夜里，弟弟轻轻关上台灯，只听一声轻响。 The lamp made a soft click in the dark room.
sceneCN: 这里 click 是「咔哒声」（第 1 个义项：短促清脆的声音）；句意是台灯在黑暗的房间里发出轻脆的咔哒声。

collocations.zh: 咔哒一声就位；豁然开朗

derivatives.zh: 由 click 加 bait 构成，义为「标题党；诱饵标题」，指吸引点击的标题
由 click  + suffix  -er 构成，义为「遥控器；翻页器」

senses.title: A short sharp sound
senses.definition: a short, light, sharp sound
senses.definitionCN: 一声短促轻脆的声音
senses.example: The door locked with a click.
senses.exampleCN: 门咔哒一声锁上了。
senses.why: Small metal parts knock together and give out this sharp little sound, so the sound got its own name.
senses.whyCN: 金属小部件相碰会发出这种脆响，这声音便有了名字。

senses.title: To press a mouse button
senses.definition: to press one of the buttons on a computer mouse
senses.definitionCN: 按下鼠标上的按键
senses.example: Click the picture to hear the song.
senses.exampleCN: 点击这张图片就能听到这首歌。
senses.why: The mouse button makes the same little sound, so the action borrowed the noise for a name.
senses.whyCN: 鼠标按键按下时发出同样的小响声，这个动作便借用了响声的名字。

senses.title: To suddenly understand or get on well
senses.definition: to become clear or friendly very suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然变得清楚或融洽
senses.example: At last the maths question clicked for me.
senses.exampleCN: 我终于一下子弄懂了那道数学题。
senses.why: When parts fit, they snap together with a click; minds and friendships can snap together the same way.
senses.whyCN: 部件合适时会咔哒一声咬合，思路和友谊也会这样一下子咬合。

intro.en: Click is a word copied from sound itself: someone heard it and wrote it down.
intro.cn: click 是从声音本身抄下来的词：有人听到了，便把它写了下来。

items.en: Click is imitative: it copies the sharp sound it names, so its roots do not lead back to Latin or Greek.
items.cn: click 是拟声词：它模仿自己所指的脆响，因此词根并不追溯到拉丁语或希腊语。

items.en: The noun click for a sharp sound is first recorded in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 表示脆响的名词 click 最早记录于十七世纪。

items.en: The verb soon followed, for things that make that sound or lock together.
items.cn: 动词随后出现，指发出这种声音或咬合的动作。

items.en: In the twentieth century the computer mouse borrowed the word for pressing its button.
items.cn: 二十世纪，计算机鼠标借用了这个词来表示按键动作。

items.en: Later still, people said something clicks when an idea or a friendship suddenly fits.
items.cn: 更晚人们用 something clicks 表示想法或友谊一下子契合。

note.en: The first group collects sound-alike and shape-alike words; the second collects related sounds and computer actions.
note.cn: 第一组收音近形近的词，第二组收相关声音和电脑操作。

entries.definition: A machine that shows the time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时钟」，与 click 只差一个字母，词源无关。

entries.definition: A small device for changing slides.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「翻页器；遥控器」，由 click 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A louder, harder knocking sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咔嗒声（较响）」，与 click 音近义近。

entries.definition: A light touch on a screen.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「轻点（屏幕）」，触屏时代的常用说法。

entries.definition: A sudden sharp breaking sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「啪嗒声；断裂声」，声音更响更硬。

entries.definition: Two quick presses of a mouse button.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「双击」，由 double 加 click 构成的电脑用语。

normalIntro.en: Remember click through the sounds and screens of daily life.
normalIntro.cn: 从日常的声音与屏幕出发记忆 click。

normal.en: click copies the sound it names: click!
normal.cn: click 模仿它所指的声音：咔哒！

normal.en: click the mouse means press the mouse button.
normal.cn: click the mouse 指按鼠标键。

normal.en: click into place means things suddenly fit.
normal.cn: click into place 指事情豁然开朗。

normal.en: clock and click differ by only one letter.
normal.cn: clock 和 click 只差一个字母。

normal.en: clickbait means a title made to get clicks.
normal.cn: clickbait 指为了骗点击而起的标题。

abstract.en: Hear the tiny snap of a seat belt locking.
abstract.cn: 听安全带扣上时那声细小的脆响。

abstract.en: Feel the mouse button sink and rise under your finger.
abstract.cn: 感受鼠标键在指尖下沉又弹起。

abstract.en: Picture a puzzle piece falling into its hole.
abstract.cn: 想象一块拼图落进它该在的凹槽。

examples.en: Hear the click of the camera before the photo.
examples.cn: 拍照前能听到相机的咔哒声。

examples.en: Click the green button to send your homework.
examples.cn: 点击绿色按钮提交作业。

examples.en: The key turned with a click and the box opened.
examples.cn: 钥匙咔哒一转，盒子打开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克利克」——鼠标一点，「克」的一声「利」落清「克」，click 就是那一声脆响。

root: 拟声词，模仿短促脆响，来源不确定 → 十七世纪首见名词 → 动词随之出现 → 现代英语扩展到鼠标点击与「一下子契合」。

sensesIntro.en: Click moves from a tiny sound to a screen action and then to minds that fit.
sensesIntro.cn: click 从一声轻响延伸到屏幕操作，再到想法的豁然开朗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two small parts meeting with one sharp sound
core.cn: 核心意象：两个小部件相碰发出一声脆响

branches.en: The sharp little sound
branches.cn: 那一声短促脆响

branches.en: Pressing a mouse button
branches.cn: 按下鼠标按键

branches.en: A sudden understanding
branches.cn: 突然的领悟

branches.en: People getting on well at once
branches.cn: 人们一拍即合

branches.en: Hands, keys and screens
branches.cn: 手、按键与屏幕

intro.en: Click builds simple, modern words around its tiny sound.
intro.cn: click 围绕它那声轻响造出简单而现代的词。

latinIntro.en: Click has no Latin root: it is pure imitation of sound.
latinIntro.cn: click 没有拉丁词根：它纯粹模仿声音。

items.meaning: a device that makes clicking sounds
items.example: The teacher used a clicker to change slides.
items.exampleCN: 老师用翻页器切换幻灯片。

items.meaning: a title made to attract clicks
two quick presses of the mouse
items.example: Double-click the file to open it.

items.meaning: the record of a user's clicks
items.exampleCN: 网站分析自己的点击流数据。

items.example: We heard the clack of heels in the hall.
items.exampleCN: 我们听到大厅里高跟鞋的咔嗒声。

items.example: The branch broke with a snap.

definition_zh: 调查；测量；勘测；概览
definition_en: a study of opinions or facts, or to look over an area
core_image: 研究员拿着问卷站在街角，记录路人的回答
scene: 研究者调查了五百名居民。 The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
sceneCN: 这里 survey 是「调查」（第 1 个义项）；句意：研究者调查了五百名居民。

derivatives.zh: 测量员
测量

senses.title: A study of opinions
senses.definition: a set of questions used to collect opinions or facts
senses.definitionCN: 用于收集意见或事实的一组问题
senses.example: The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者调查了五百名居民。
senses.why: This is the common social-science sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是常见的社会科学义项。

senses.title: The measuring of land
senses.definition: the act of measuring land or an area
senses.definitionCN: 测量土地或区域的行为
senses.example: They surveyed the land before building.

senses.title: The passage of time
senses.definition: the continuous progress of seconds, hours, and years in which events occur
senses.definitionCN: 事件在其中发生的秒、小时、年的连续流逝
senses.example: Time passes more slowly when you are waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 等待时时间过得格外慢。
senses.why: Old English tima named a limited or allotted period; extending it indefinitely gives the modern sense of time itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 tima 指一段有限、被分配的时间；把它无限延展便成了现代的「时间本身」。

senses.title: A particular moment
senses.definition: a specific point or moment at which something happens
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的具体时刻
senses.example: It is time to go home.
senses.exampleCN: 该回家了。
senses.why: A point inside the stream of time is itself a small allotted piece of it.
senses.whyCN: 时间之流中的一处，本身就是一小段被分配的时间。

senses.title: An occasion or instance
senses.definition: one occasion on which something happens, counted with a number
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的一次，与数词连用计数
senses.example: This is the third time she has called.
senses.exampleCN: 这是她第三次打电话来。
senses.why: Each separate span of time becomes a countable unit, so repetition is counted in times.
senses.whyCN: 每一段独立的时间成可数单位，重复便以 times 计数。

senses.title: A period of history
senses.definition: a stretch of years associated with a distinct way of life or a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 与某种生活方式或某位统治者相关的一段年代
senses.example: In Roman times the road carried soldiers and grain.
senses.exampleCN: 在罗马时代，这条路上运送着士兵与粮食。
senses.why: Large allotted spans of history are time on the grandest scale.
senses.whyCN: 历史上被划出的大段时间，是最大尺度的时间。

senses.title: A suitable moment
senses.definition: a moment favourable for a particular action
senses.definitionCN: 适合某种行动的时刻
senses.example: Now is the time to ask for help.
senses.exampleCN: 现在是求助的时机。
senses.why: If time is allotted, some of it is given for a purpose, and that purpose opens a window.
senses.whyCN: 如果时间是分配的，其中总有一段给了某个目的，那段就是窗口。

senses.title: To measure how long something takes
senses.definition: to measure or record the duration of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 测量或记录某项活动的时长
senses.example: The coach timed every runner with a stopwatch.
senses.exampleCN: 教练用秒表给每位跑者计时。
senses.why: Telling time turns the noun into the act of counting the passing units.
senses.whyCN: 读取时间把名词变成了数过单位的行为。

senses.title: To schedule at a moment
senses.definition: to arrange for something to happen at a planned moment
senses.definitionCN: 安排某事在计划好的时刻发生
senses.example: They timed the launch for early morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把发布会定在清早。
senses.why: To give a portion of time to an event is to decide its allotted moment.
senses.whyCN: 把一段时间分给某个事件，就是决定它被分配的时刻。

senses.title: Times of rhythm or music
senses.definition: the rhythm or speed of a piece of music, or the beat of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 乐曲的节奏或速度，也指活动的节拍
senses.example: The drummer set the time for the whole band.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓手为整个乐队定下节拍。
senses.why: Music measures time in equal beats, so the word names the very beat it counts.
senses.whyCN: 音乐以等分的拍计量时间，于是本词也被赋予它所数的那一拍。

senses.title: Times as multiplication
senses.definition: used after a number to show repeated quantity in multiplication
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字后表示乘法中的倍数
senses.example: Four times five is twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 四乘五等于二十。
senses.why: When a span repeats a number of times, counting it multiplies; hence the arithmetic sense.
senses.whyCN: 当一段时间重复若干次，计数就变成相乘，于是有了算术义。

senses.title: Time on a clock
senses.definition: the reading shown by a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 钟表显示的读数
senses.example: The clocks in the shop kept different time.
senses.exampleCN: 店里的钟各走各的时间。
senses.why: A clock exists to convert the invisible stream into a number we can read.
senses.whyCN: 钟表的存在就是把看不见的流动变成可读的数字。

intro.en: The English noun is native, related to words in other Germanic languages for a time or hour, and its root sense is an allotted or divided period.

items.en: The noun expands from a limited span to time in general and to counted occasions.

items.en: The verb to time, meaning to measure or schedule, is formed from the noun.

items.en: Clock and railway keeping time fix the phrase as a standard of accuracy.
items.cn: 钟表与铁路的「对时间」让这一短语成为准确性的标准。

items.en: The sense of dating from a clock, and of rhythm in music, settle as ordinary uses.

note.cn: 形近组收集以 time 为词干构成的词族，近义组列出表示时段与计时的其他词。

senses.example: He works as a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他的工作是老师。
senses.why: A person standing on the same level as a role is described by that role, which gives as meaning in the role of.
senses.whyCN: 一个人与某个角色处在同一位置，就用那个角色来描述他，于是 as 表示「作为」。

senses.title: At the time when
senses.definition: at the same time that something happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生的同一时间
senses.example: As I walked home, it began to rain.
senses.exampleCN: 我走回家时，天开始下雨。
senses.why: Two events on one level in time are joined by the same word, which gives the sense of while.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上处于同一水平的两个事件也用同一个词连接，于是有「当……时」。

senses.title: Because
senses.definition: for the reason that
senses.definitionCN: 由于某个原因
senses.example: As it was late, we took a taxi.
senses.exampleCN: 因为时间晚了，我们坐了出租车。
senses.why: A reason standing beside a result is also lined up with it, which gives the sense of because.
senses.whyCN: 原因与结果并列在一起，也是被摆在同一水平上，于是有「因为」。

definition_zh: 意见；看法；评价；舆论
definition_en: what a person thinks about something, a judgement offered as advice, or the body of views held by many people
core_image: 一张对折的纸片被摊开，上面是某人用笔写下的一句话，墨迹还有一点湿
scene: 夏夜的阳台上，两个人靠着栏杆聊到很晚，一个说出自己的判断，另一个只是听着，没有立刻反驳。 In her opinion, the plan needs more time before it can work.
sceneCN: 这里的 opinion 是「看法、意见」（第 1 个义项：个人对事情的判断）；句意为依她看，这个方案还需要更多时间才能奏效。图中可辨识物件：阳台栏杆、写字的纸片。

collocations.zh: 看法问题；见仁见智的事

derivatives.zh: 由 opinion 加 -ated 构成，义为「固执己见的；自负的」
由 opinionated 加 -ness 构成，义为「固执己见的性情」
由 opinion 与 poll 复合而成，义为「民意调查」

senses.title: What a person thinks about something
senses.definition: a belief or judgement that a person forms about a matter, without claiming it is a proven fact
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对某事形成的看法或判断，并不宣称它已被证实为事实
senses.example: In my opinion, the meeting could have been shorter.
senses.exampleCN: 依我看，这次会议本可以开得更短。
senses.why: The Latin verb opinari meant to think or suppose, so the noun starts as the act of holding a view in one's mind rather than as knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 opinari 意为「以为、揣度」，所以这个名词的起点是心里抱着一种看法，而不是已经掌握的知识。

senses.title: A judgement given as advice
senses.definition: a considered view offered by someone whose knowledge is being asked for, as in a second opinion
senses.definitionCN: 由具备相关知识的人给出、供人参考的判断，如另请人再作一次评估
senses.example: The doctor suggested she get a second opinion before the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议她在手术前再找一位同行评估。
senses.why: Once a view is worth consulting, the word shifts from private belief to a judgement that carries a specialist's weight.
senses.whyCN: 一种看法一旦值得专门请教，这个词便从私人的信念转成带有专业分量的判断。

senses.title: The views held by many people together
senses.definition: the general body of views held by the public at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期公众整体所持的各种看法
senses.example: Public opinion turned against the new tax within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 不到一个月，公众舆论就转而反对这项新税。
senses.why: Many private views, counted together, become a force of their own, and English lets the same word name that collective weight.
senses.whyCN: 许多私人的看法汇在一起，就成了独立的力量，英语便用同一个词来指这份集体的分量。

senses.title: A point on which people differ
senses.titleCN: 看法问题；见仁见智的事
senses.definition: a matter that cannot be settled by evidence alone because it depends on how people judge it
senses.definitionCN: 仅凭证据无法定论、要靠各人如何判断的事情
senses.example: Whether the film is funny is a matter of opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影好不好笑，是个见仁见智的问题。
senses.why: If a view is not proof, then some questions cannot be closed by facts, and the word marks that limit openly.
senses.whyCN: 既然看法不等于证据，那么有些问题就无法靠事实了结，这个词恰好在提醒这条界线。

intro.en: Opinion came to English from Latin through French, and it began as a verb of thinking rather than a noun of belief; the family keeps that sense of judging without proof.
intro.cn: opinion 经法语由拉丁语进入英语，起初来自表示「思考」的动词而非表示「信念」的名词；这一族词始终保留「无确证而判断」的意味。

items.en: Opinari meant to think, suppose or believe, and it described the mind taking a position before certainty was reached.
items.cn: opinari 意为思考、揣度、相信，描写头脑在尚未确定之前先站到一个位置上。

items.en: The noun opinio grew from that verb and named a belief held in the mind, often in contrast with knowledge or proof.
items.cn: 名词 opinio 由该动词生长出来，指心中所抱的看法，常与知识或证据相对照。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as opinion, meaning what one thinks or what people generally think, and it entered English with both readings.
items.cn: 古法语以 opinion 承袭该名词，既指个人所想，也指众人所想，进入英语时两种读法都在。

items.en: Middle English used opinion for personal views, for expert judgements and for the general voice of the people.
items.cn: 中古英语把 opinion 用于个人看法、专家判断，以及民众的一般声音。

items.en: Modern English keeps opinion for stated beliefs, for consulted advice and for public sentiment, and adds fixed phrases such as in my opinion and a matter of opinion.
items.cn: 现代英语让 opinion 兼指说出的信念、请教得来的意见与公众情绪，并固定下 in my opinion、a matter of opinion 之类的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of thinking and judging; the near-meaning group collects other names for a view held about something.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「思考、判断」词干上的词；近义组收其他表示对某事所持看法的名称。

entries.definition: To state a view, often in a formal or slightly stiff tone.
entries.definitionCN: 说出看法，常带正式或略生硬的语气。

entries.definition: Holding views too firmly and unwilling to listen.
entries.definitionCN: 过于坚持己见、不肯听别人的。

entries.definition: Open to debate because no proof can settle it.
entries.definitionCN: 因无证据可定论而可以争论的。

entries.definition: The way a person sees or regards a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人看待某事的眼光或角度。

entries.definition: Something accepted as true, often without proof.
entries.definitionCN: 常指未经证明而被当作真实接受的东西。

entries.definition: A decision reached after weighing the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 权衡事实之后作出的判断。

entries.definition: A settled position taken toward an issue.
entries.definitionCN: 对某一问题所采取的既定立场。

normalIntro.en: Opinion is a Latin thinking-verb turned noun, so the hooks follow the act of the mind taking a position rather than any object in the world.
normalIntro.cn: opinion 是拉丁语「思考」动词变来的名词，所以记忆钩子顺着头脑站定位置的动作走，而不是顺着世上的物件走。

normal.en: The Latin verb opinari means to think or suppose, and opinio is simply the noun made from it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 opinari 意为思考、揣度，opinio 就是由它造出的名词。

normal.en: In my opinion is the phrase that shows the word's honesty: the speaker marks the statement as a view, not a fact.
normal.cn: in my opinion 这句搭配正显出这个词的诚实：说话人把话标成看法，而不是事实。

normal.en: A second opinion is a judgement invited from another expert, which is why the word can mean advice as well as belief.
normal.cn: a second opinion 是另请一位专家给出的判断，所以这个词除了信念也能指意见。

normal.en: Opinionated adds a suffix of possession: a person so full of opinions that listening stops.
normal.cn: opinionated 加的是表示「充满」的词尾：一个人满到自己都听不进别人的话。

normal.en: Public opinion is private views counted together, so the word moves from one head to a whole crowd.
normal.cn: public opinion 是把私人看法合起来数，于是这个词从一个脑袋走到一整群人。

abstract.en: A word built on not knowing is the honest companion of every argument, because it leaves room for the other side.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「尚未确知」之上的词，是一切争论的诚实伙伴，因为它给对方留了位置。

abstract.en: Opinion and fact live beside each other, and much of daily speech is spent sorting which is which.
abstract.cn: 看法与事实并排而立，日常说话有大半时间都用在校准哪句是哪类。

abstract.en: When many opinions agree, they stop sounding like opinions and start sounding like the weather.
abstract.cn: 当许多看法彼此一致，它们就不再像看法，而开始像天气一样被谈论。

examples.en: In my opinion, the plan needs more time.
examples.cn: 依我看，这个方案还需要更多时间。

examples.en: Public opinion changed quickly after the report.
examples.cn: 报告公布之后，公众舆论很快转变。

examples.en: The doctor asked her to seek a second opinion.
examples.cn: 医生请她再去求一份专业意见。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a view held without proof; the senses divide by who holds it and how much weight it carries, from one person's belief to expert advice to the public voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是未经确证而持有的看法；义项按持有者与分量分出，从个人信念，到专业意见，再到公众声音。

core.cn: 核心意象：一张对折的纸片被摊开，上面是某人用笔写下的一句话，墨迹还有一点湿。

branches.cn: 两个人在阳台上聊到很晚

branches.en: a patient asking another doctor to look again
branches.cn: 病人请另一位医生再看一次

branches.en: a crowd changing its mind after a report
branches.cn: 一群人读了报告后改变想法

branches.en: a debate that facts alone cannot close
branches.cn: 仅凭事实无法了结的争论

branches.en: the same private view growing into a public force
branches.cn: 同一种私人看法长成公共力量

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of thinking with a noun ending attached; English then adds endings that mark a person too fond of views and a matter open to dispute.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「思考」动词接上名词词尾而成；英语随后又加上词尾，用来指过分爱持看法的人，以及可供争论的事。

latinIntro.en: Latin opinari, opinio and opinabilis are recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry behind its English forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 opinari、opinio、opinabilis 均有记录，因此这一族英语词形背后有可靠的拉丁语世系。

definition_zh: 支付；付钱；值得；薪水
definition_en: to give money in return for goods or work; also to bring a good result, and the money received for a job
core_image: 一只手把钱推过柜台，另一只手把东西递回来
scene: 深夜的小餐馆里，服务员把账单放在桌角。 He paid the bill and left a tip under the cup.
sceneCN: 这里是「支付、付钱」（第 1 个义项：为商品或服务付款）；句意为他付了账单，还把零钱压在杯子下面。图中可辨识物件：账单夹、咖啡杯、收银台的小灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 pay 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，指付款这一行为或付出的款项
由 pay 加 -able 构成，指应付的、可支付的
由 pay 加表示「做某事的人」的 -er 构成，指付款人
由 pay 加表示「受事者」的 -ee 构成，指收款人

senses.title: To give money for something
senses.definition: to give someone money in return for goods, work or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为货物、劳动或服务把钱交给对方
senses.example: She paid for the tickets with her phone.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手机付了票钱。
senses.why: The Latin root meant to pacify, and handing over money was seen as calming the person who was owed, so payment began as an act of settling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「使平静」，把钱交出去被看作让被欠的一方平静下来，所以付款最初是一种平息。

senses.title: To be worth the effort
senses.definition: to bring a benefit that is worth the cost or effort involved
senses.definitionCN: 带来足以抵过所付代价或力气的好处
senses.example: It pays to read the instructions first.
senses.exampleCN: 先读说明是值得的。
senses.why: If money paid can settle a debt, then any effort can be said to pay when it returns something worth more than it cost.
senses.whyCN: 既然付出的钱可以结清债务，那么任何力气只要能换回超过代价的东西，也可以说它 pay。

senses.title: Money received for work
senses.definition: the money that someone receives for the work they do
senses.definitionCN: 因工作而得到的报酬
senses.example: The pay is low, but the hours are short.
senses.exampleCN: 工资不高，但工时短。
senses.why: The verb names the act of handing money over; turned into a noun, it names the money that arrives on the other side of the same exchange.
senses.whyCN: 动词指把钱交出去的动作；变成名词后，它指同一场交换里流到另一边的钱。

senses.title: To suffer a cost
senses.definition: to experience something unpleasant as a result of what one has done
senses.definitionCN: 因自己做过的事而承受不愉快的后果
senses.example: He paid dearly for that careless remark.
senses.exampleCN: 他为那句轻率的话付出了很大代价。
senses.why: Once pay means to give up something for a result, the thing given up need not be money, so a mistake can be paid for with pain or time.
senses.whyCN: 当 pay 表示为了结果交出东西，交出的就不必是钱，于是错误也可以用痛苦或时间来偿还。

intro.en: Pay goes back to a Latin word for peace, and it reached English through French with the practical sense of settling what is owed.
intro.cn: pay 可以追溯到拉丁语中表示和平的词，经法语进入英语时带上了「结清所欠」的实际含义。

items.en: Pax meant peace, and a dispute that had been settled was imagined as quiet after conflict.
items.cn: pax 意为和平，被平息下来的争端被想象成冲突之后的安静。

items.en: The verb pacare meant to make peaceful or to quiet someone, and it could describe calming an angry creditor.
items.cn: 动词 pacare 意为使平静、安抚某人，也可以形容安抚愤怒的债主。

items.en: In medieval Latin the verb took the practical sense of satisfying a debt, so money quieted a person the way peace quieted a quarrel.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语里，这个动词获得了「清偿债务」的实际含义：钱让人平息，正如和平让争吵平息。

items.en: Old French payer carried that sense of satisfying someone with money, and Anglo-French carried it into law and trade.
items.cn: 古法语 payer 承下用钱让人满足的含义，盎格鲁法语又把它带进法律与商业。

items.en: Middle English payen becomes modern pay, with the irregular past paid, and the noun pay for the money earned.
items.cn: 中古英语 payen 变成现代 pay，过去式是不规则的 paid，名词 pay 则指挣到的钱。

entries.definitionCN: 那个拉丁词根所指的安宁、无冲突状态。

entries.definition: To pay what is owed and so close an account.
entries.definitionCN: 付清欠款从而结清账目。

entries.definition: Money paid to a worker, usually by the hour or the day.
entries.definitionCN: 付给工人的报酬，通常按小时或按天计。

entries.definition: A fixed amount paid to an employee each month or year.
entries.definitionCN: 按月或按年付给雇员的固定报酬。

entries.definition: Money paid for a service or for the right to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项服务或某项权利付出的费用。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of a Latin noun for peace, and its history is the story of turning money into quiet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语中表示和平的名词长出来，它的历史就是把钱变成安静的过程。

normal.en: The Latin word for peace is pax, and it is the seed of pay: to pay was to make a creditor peaceful.
normal.cn: 表示和平的拉丁词是 pax，它就是 pay 的种子：付钱原本是让债主平静下来。

normal.en: Pacare means to quiet someone, so payment is a kind of calming carried out with money.
normal.cn: pacare 意为使人平静，所以付款是一种用钱完成的安抚。

normal.en: The past tense is paid, not payed, because the word came through French instead of being built inside English.
normal.cn: 过去式是 paid 而不是 payed，因为它经法语传来，不是英语自己造的。

normal.en: Pay attention uses the same verb for giving something invisible: you hand over your notice.
normal.cn: pay attention 用同一个动词表示给出无形的东西：你把注意力交出去。

normal.en: A payer sends money and a payee receives it, so the suffixes -er and -ee point in opposite directions.
normal.cn: payer 付钱，payee 收钱，后缀 -er 与 -ee 的方向正好相反。

abstract.en: Every payment begins as a promise, which is why the root of the word means peace rather than money.
abstract.cn: 每一笔付款最初都是一个承诺，所以这个词的词根表示和平，而不是钱。

abstract.en: The word treats a debt as a small quarrel that money can quiet.
abstract.cn: 这个词把债务看成一场小争吵，钱可以让它安静下来。

abstract.en: Pay is the point where effort and reward are weighed against each other on the same scale.
abstract.cn: pay 是力气与回报被放在同一杆秤上互相衡量的那个点。

examples.en: She paid for the tickets with her phone.
examples.cn: 她用手机付了票钱。

examples.en: It pays to read the instructions first.
examples.cn: 先读说明是值得的。

examples.en: The pay is low, but the hours are short.
examples.cn: 工资不高，但工时短。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赔」——把钱付出去，像赔给别人一样；pay 就是支付。

root: 拉丁语 pax（和平）→ pacare（使平静、清偿）→ 中世纪拉丁语「偿还债主」→ 古法语 payer → 英语 pay；同族词多与「平息、付清」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is handing over money to quiet a claim; from that act come the sense of worth, the noun for wages, and the wider cost paid for a mistake.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把钱交出去让索求平息；由这个动作分出「值得」、表示工资的名词，以及为错误付出的更大代价。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把钱推过柜台，另一只手把东西递回来。

branches.cn: 同一个动词在衡量所得与所失

definition_zh: 出售；推销；卖得
definition_en: to give something in exchange for money, to persuade people to buy something, or to be bought in a certain way
core_image: 集市刚开，摊主把一筐番茄摆到最前面
scene: 集市刚开，摊主就把番茄摆到最前面。 They sell fresh vegetables every morning.

senses.title: Give for money
senses.definition: to give something to someone in exchange for money
senses.definitionCN: 用某物换取金钱
senses.example: He sold his old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧自行车卖了。
senses.why: This is the basic commercial sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的交易义。

senses.title: Persuade to buy
senses.definition: to make something seem worth buying
senses.definitionCN: 使某物看起来值得购买
senses.example: The ad sells the idea of a simple life.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告推销的是一种简单生活的理念。
senses.why: Selling can also mean promoting an idea.
senses.whyCN: sell 也可以指推销一种理念。

senses.title: Be bought
senses.definition: to be bought in a particular way or amount
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式或数量被买走
senses.example: The book sold a million copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书卖出了上百万册。
senses.why: The intransitive use describes sales figures.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法描述销售情况。

intro.en: Sell comes from Old English sellan, to give or hand over, with the past form sold.
intro.cn: sell 源自古英语 sellan（给予、交出），过去式为 sold。

items.en: Sellan meant to give or hand over.
items.cn: sellan 意为给予或交出。

items.en: The past form sealde later became sold.
items.cn: 过去式 sealde 后来演变为 sold。

items.en: The verb narrowed toward selling goods.
items.cn: 该动词的意义收窄到出售货物。

items.en: Sell out named all goods being taken.
items.cn: sell out 指货物全部卖出。

items.en: Marketing extended sell to ideas and images.
items.cn: 营销把 sell 扩展到理念与形象。

note.en: Sell is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs of trade.
note.cn: 把 sell 与形近词以及表示交易的动词作比较。

abstract.en: What sells easily is not always what lasts.

definition_zh: 第八；八分之一
definition_en: coming after seven others in order, or one part of eight equal parts
core_image: 八车道的第八条跑道线
scene: 操场跑道画着整齐的白线，发令枪还没响。 She waited at the eighth lane.
sceneCN: 这里 eighth 是「第八条」（第 1 个义项：序数位次）；句意是她在第八条跑道等候。图中可辨识物件：跑道、白线、等候的选手、发令台。

senses.title: Position 8 in a series
senses.definition: coming after seven others in order
senses.definitionCN: 排在七个之后的位置。
senses.example: She waited at the eighth lane.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第八条跑道等候。
senses.why: The ordinal suffix -th turns eight into a position word just as -st turns one into first.
senses.whyCN: -th 后缀把 eight 变成位置词，正如 -st 把 one 变成 first。

senses.title: One of eight equal parts
senses.definition: one part when a whole is divided into eight equal parts
senses.definitionCN: 整体分成八等份中的一份。
senses.example: He sold an eighth of his shares.
senses.exampleCN: 他卖掉了自己股份的八分之一。
senses.why: Ordinals name fractions by convention, so eighth doubles as the share itself.
senses.whyCN: 序数按惯例兼指分数，eighth 便同时指份额。

senses.title: An eighth note in music
senses.definition: a musical note lasting half as long as a quarter note
senses.definitionCN: 时值为四分音符一半的音符。
senses.example: The melody races through eighth notes.
senses.exampleCN: 旋律用八分音符快速掠过。
senses.why: Music borrowed the fraction system for note lengths, so eighth names a duration.
senses.whyCN: 音乐借用分数体系标注时值，eighth 就成了一种时长。

intro.en: Eighth is eight plus the oldest ordinal ending in the language.
intro.cn: eighth 是 eight 加上英语最古老的序数词尾。

items.en: Old English eahtoða, with the regular ordinal suffix, meant eighth.
items.cn: 古英语 eahtoða，带规则序数后缀，意为「第八」。

items.en: Proto-Germanic ahtudô carried the same suffix family seen in Gothic.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 ahtudô 携带与哥特语相同的后缀家族。

items.en: Middle English eigthe lost its middle vowel and settled toward eighth.
items.cn: 中古英语 eigthe 失去中间元音，向 eighth 靠拢。

items.en: Modern English spells it eighth with silent gh and one crisp th sound.
items.cn: 现代英语拼作 eighth，gh 不发音，只留下一个清脆的 th。

items.en: Musical usage like eighth note entered later through fraction vocabulary.
items.cn: eighth note 等音乐用语借分数词汇在近代进入英语。

note.en: Two small groups: the numbers that sound like eighth and the terms around it.
note.cn: 两组小集合：与 eighth 音近的词及其周边术语。

definition_zh: 垃圾；废物；蹩脚货；丢弃；捣毁
definition_en: things thrown away because they are no longer wanted, or to throw such things away or destroy them
core_image: 楼道口一只鼓鼓的垃圾袋，袋口露出几根果皮
scene: 清晨，环卫车沿街收走门口一袋袋垃圾，纸箱被压扁堆在路边。 Please take the trash out before you leave.
sceneCN: 这里 trash 是「垃圾」（第 1 个义项：扔掉的废弃物）；句意为走之前把垃圾拿出去。门口那一袋袋东西正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -y 构成形容词，义为「劣质的；低俗的」
复合名词，义为「垃圾桶」（美式）
现在分词名词化，义为「捣毁；痛批」

senses.title: Things thrown away
senses.definition: things that are no longer wanted and are thrown out
senses.definitionCN: 不再需要、被扔掉的东西
senses.example: The kitchen trash smells in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天厨房的垃圾会有味道。
senses.why: The word began as a name for broken twigs and dry leaves, the stuff that falls and is swept up.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指折断的细枝与枯叶，即落下后被扫走的东西。

senses.title: Something of poor quality
senses.definition: things or work that are worthless or of very low quality
senses.definitionCN: 没有价值或质量极差的东西或作品
senses.example: The film is pure trash.
senses.exampleCN: 这部片子完全是垃圾。
senses.why: If what is thrown away is worthless, anything worthless can be called trash.
senses.whyCN: 既然扔掉的东西没有价值，任何没价值的东西都能叫 trash。

senses.title: To throw something away
senses.definition: to get rid of something as useless
senses.definitionCN: 把某物当作无用之物处理掉
senses.example: Trash the old receipts once they are checked.
senses.exampleCN: 旧收据核对完就扔掉。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb when the action of discarding is what needs naming.
senses.whyCN: 当需要给「抛弃」这个动作起名时，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: To damage or destroy badly
senses.definition: to wreck a place or attack something severely
senses.definitionCN: 把地方砸坏，或把某物批得体无完肤
senses.example: Fans trashed the hall after the show.
senses.exampleCN: 演出结束后粉丝把礼堂砸了。
senses.why: Treating something as trash is the same as destroying it, so the verb widens to wrecking.
senses.whyCN: 把东西当垃圾处理就等于毁掉它，于是动词扩展到「砸烂」。

senses.title: To criticise harshly
senses.definition: to write or speak about something very unfavourably
senses.definitionCN: 极不客气地评论某物
senses.example: Every critic trashed the new play.
senses.exampleCN: 每个评论家都痛批这出新戏。
senses.why: When a review throws a work away in words, the verb for discarding fits the judging.
senses.whyCN: 当评论用文字把作品扔掉时，表示丢弃的这个动词正好贴合那种评判。

intro.en: The word is of uncertain origin, first naming broken twigs and dry leaves, then any rubbish.
intro.cn: 这个词来源不确定，最早指折断的细枝与枯叶，后来泛指一切废物。

items.en: The word appears in the sixteenth century as a name for withered leaves and twigs.
items.cn: 这个词在十六世纪出现，指枯叶与细枝。

items.en: American usage of the nineteenth century widens trash to household rubbish.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国用法把 trash 扩大到家庭垃圾。

items.en: Rubbish, garbage, and trash divide the work differently in British and American English.
items.cn: rubbish、garbage 与 trash 在英式与美式英语里分工不同。

items.en: The verb sense of destroying a place spreads through journalism in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 动词「砸坏一个地方」的义项在二十世纪经新闻传播开来。

items.en: The word now also covers poor quality in films, music, and writing.
items.cn: 如今这个词也涵盖电影、音乐与写作的低劣之作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that look close, while the near-meaning group names other kinds of waste.
note.cn: 形近组汇集外形接近的短词，近义组列出其他废弃物的说法。

normal.en: Three letters and one sh sound, harsh like a bin lid.
normal.cn: 三个字母，一声 sh，脆得像垃圾桶盖合上。

normal.en: Trash can is American; British speakers more often say rubbish bin.
normal.cn: trash can 是美式，英式多说 rubbish bin。

normal.en: The verb trashes a room, and the noun names what is left.
normal.cn: 动词把房间砸烂，名词指的是留下的一地。

normal.en: Trashy adds -y to make an adjective of poor quality.
normal.cn: trashy 加 -y 成为「劣质」的形容词。

normal.en: A short, blunt word, suited to a quick shove.
normal.cn: 短而硬的词，正配随手一推的动作。

abstract.en: Picture a bin bag split at the corner of a stairwell.
abstract.cn: 想象楼道口一只裂了口的垃圾袋。

abstract.en: Smell it on a hot morning and the word sticks.
abstract.cn: 在热天早晨闻一闻，这个词就记住了。

abstract.en: Then hear a critic say the same word about a play.
abstract.cn: 再听评论家用同一个词评一出戏。

examples.en: Put the trash out on Tuesday night.
examples.cn: 周二晚上把垃圾拿出去。

examples.en: Do not trash the hotel room.
examples.cn: 不要把酒店房间弄得一团糟。

examples.en: Some of that music is real trash.
examples.cn: 那些音乐里有不少真是糟粕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抓什」——抓到什么都往垃圾堆里扔。

root: 来源不确定，十六世纪指枯枝落叶，后泛指垃圾；同族有 trashy、trashcan

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with what is swept up and ends with what is thrown away in words.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从被扫起来的东西开始，一路走到被文字判掉的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bulging bin bag at the foot of the stairs.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼梯脚下一只鼓鼓的垃圾袋。

branches.en: The plain sense of household waste.
branches.cn: 最朴素义：家庭垃圾。

branches.en: The quality sense, where worthless things are meant.
branches.cn: 品质义：指的是没价值的东西。

branches.en: The verb senses: throw away, then wreck.
branches.cn: 动词义：先扔掉，再砸烂。

branches.en: The reviewing sense, where a work is thrown away in print.
branches.cn: 评论义：作品在纸上被扔掉。

branches.en: The bin sense, the everyday picture of the word.
branches.cn: 垃圾桶义：这个词最日常的画面。

intro.en: The word has no useful Latin pieces, but its English family is easy to see.
intro.cn: 这个词没有可用的拉丁部件，但它的英语词族很容易看出。

latinIntro.en: The stem trash- appears in trashy, trashcan, and trashing.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 trash- 出现在 trashy、trashcan 与 trashing 里。

items.example: The stem is the whole noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干就是名词的全部。
trash 加 can 成为 trashcan。

items.example: The trashing of the site caused anger.
items.exampleCN: 对场地的捣毁引发了愤怒。

items.example: Garbage goes in the other bin.

latinEntries.meaning: withered leaves and twigs, then rubbish

definition_zh: 举起；提高；筹集；抚养；提出；引起
definition_en: to lift something to a higher position; to increase an amount or level; to collect money for a purpose; to bring up children or animals; to put a subject forward for discussion; to cause a feeling or reaction
core_image: 一只举到半空的手，掌心朝前
scene: 会议室里，一位成员把手举到半空，示意想就预算发问。 She raised her hand and waited for the chair to notice her.
sceneCN: 这里 raise 是「举起」（第 1 个义项：把某物抬到更高的位置）；句意为她举起手，等主席注意到她。画面里可留意：举到半空的手、朝前的手掌、会议桌。

pos.zh: 举起；提高；筹集；抚养；提出；引起

derivatives.zh: raise 加 -er，指筹集者或饲养者
raise 加 -ing，指举起、抚养或筹集的过程
fund 与 raiser 复合，指筹款活动或筹款人

senses.title: To lift to a higher position
senses.definition: to move something upward to a higher place or level
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向上移到更高的位置或水平
senses.example: Raise your hand if you have a question.
senses.exampleCN: 有问题请举手。
senses.why: The word came into English from Old Norse with the plain sense of setting something upright or lifting it, and that physical act is still the centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古诺斯语进入英语，本义是把某物立起或抬起，这个身体动作至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To increase an amount
senses.definition: to make a price, level or amount higher
senses.definitionCN: 使价格、水平或数量变高
senses.example: The shop raised its prices twice this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店今年两次提价。
senses.why: Raising a thing higher and raising a number higher use the same image, so the word moved easily from objects to quantities.
senses.whyCN: 把东西举高与把数字提高用的是同一幅画面，所以这个词从实物轻易地转向了数量。

senses.title: To collect money
senses.definition: to gather money or support for a purpose, often for charity
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的募集钱款或支持，常指慈善
senses.example: The class raised money for the animal shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 全班为动物收容所筹集了钱款。
senses.why: Money that is brought together and lifted into a common fund looks like something raised up from many hands.
senses.whyCN: 把分散的钱聚拢并抬进一个共同基金，看起来就像从许多只手中把东西举起来。

senses.title: To bring up children or animals
senses.definition: to care for a child or an animal until it is grown
senses.definitionCN: 照料孩子或动物直到长大
senses.example: She raised three children on her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。
senses.why: To raise a child is to lift that person up through years of care, and the same verb serves for animals on a farm.
senses.whyCN: 抚养孩子就是通过多年照料把人「托举」起来，同一个动词也用于农场里的动物。

senses.title: To put a subject forward
senses.definition: to bring a question or subject to other people's attention for discussion
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或话题提到别人面前供讨论
senses.example: He raised a question about the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 他就日程安排提了一个问题。
senses.why: A subject brought into a conversation is lifted into view, so the word of lifting also means to mention for discussion.
senses.whyCN: 被带进对话的话题被举到众人眼前，于是「举起」这个词也指提出来讨论。

senses.title: To cause a feeling or reaction
senses.definition: to produce a feeling, doubt or reaction in people
senses.definitionCN: 在人们心中产生某种感受、疑虑或反应
senses.example: The news raised fears of another delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这则消息引起了对再次延误的担忧。
senses.why: If an action lifts a feeling into notice, it causes that feeling, and this sense extends the word from things to emotions.
senses.whyCN: 一个举动把某种情绪举到众人注意之中，就是引起了那种情绪，这一义项把词从实物扩展到情感。

intro.en: Raise came into English from Old Norse, where the verb meant to set something upright; it is related to rise but carries an object.
intro.cn: raise 从古诺斯语进入英语，那个动词意为把某物立起；它与 rise 相关，但必须带宾语。

items.en: Reisa meant to raise or to set upright, and Norse settlers brought it into northern English.
items.cn: reisa 意为举起或立起，诺斯定居者把它带入英格兰北部。

items.en: Raise and rise come from the same family, but rise is what a thing does and raise is what someone does to it.
items.cn: raise 与 rise 同属一族，但 rise 是事物自身发生的动作，raise 是某人对它施加的动作。

items.en: Middle English raise kept the sense of lifting and setting up, and added the sense of bringing up a child.
items.cn: 中古英语的 raise 保留了举起与竖立的意思，并增加了抚养孩子的义项。

items.en: From lifting objects came lifting prices, collecting money, raising a subject and raising a feeling.
items.cn: 从举物生出提价、筹钱、提出话题与引起情绪等义。

items.en: Modern English uses raise for lifting, increasing, collecting, nurturing, mentioning and causing, and as a noun for a pay increase.
items.cn: 现代英语用 raise 表示举起、增加、筹集、养育、提及与引起，并作名词指加薪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of lifting and increasing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根上的形式；近义组收表示举起与增加的动词。

entries.definition: To go upward by itself, without an object.
entries.definitionCN: 自身向上移动，不带宾语。

entries.definition: To begin to exist, especially of a problem.
A person or thing that raises.
The act of lifting, collecting or bringing up.
entries.definitionCN: 举起、筹集或抚养的行为。

entries.definition: To move something upward with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地把某物向上移动。

entries.definition: To make or become larger in amount.
To gather things or money together.
To care for someone while they grow.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人成长过程中给予照料。

normalIntro.en: The word always needs an object: someone raises something, whether a hand, a price, money, a child, a question or a fear.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词总要带宾语：某人把某样东西举起，无论是手、价格、钱款、孩子、问题还是恐惧。

normal.en: Raise needs an object and rise does not: you raise your hand, but the sun rises.
normal.cn: raise 需要宾语而 rise 不需要：你举起手，而太阳自己升起。

normal.en: A pay raise in American English is what British English calls a pay rise.
normal.cn: 美式英语的 a pay raise 就是英式英语的 a pay rise。

normal.en: Raise money means collect it, while raise prices means increase them: the same verb, two directions of lift.
normal.cn: raise money 是筹集，raise prices 是提高：同一个动词，两种「抬升」方向。

normal.en: Raise children and raise animals both mean care for them until grown.
normal.cn: raise children 与 raise animals 都指照料其长大。

normal.en: Raise a question is to bring it up, not to answer it.
normal.cn: raise a question 是把问题提出来，而不是回答它。

abstract.en: Almost everything people do to improve a situation can be said with this one verb, which is why it appears so often in meetings.
abstract.cn: 人们为改善处境所做的几乎每件事都能用这一个动词表达，所以它在会议里出现得如此频繁。

abstract.en: To raise a child is to lift someone you cannot fully control, and that is the daily risk of parenting.
abstract.cn: 抚养孩子就是托举一个你无法完全掌控的人，这正是养育的日常风险。

abstract.en: A question raised is a question someone must now carry, even if nobody answers it.
abstract.cn: 一个被提出的问题，就成了某人必须背负的问题，即使没有人回答。

examples.en: He raised the box above his head and held it there.
examples.cn: 他把箱子举过头顶，稳稳停在那里。

examples.en: The government plans to raise the minimum wage next year.
examples.cn: 政府计划明年提高最低工资。

examples.en: They raised enough money to rebuild the bridge.
examples.cn: 他们筹到了足够的钱重建那座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞兹」——把东西锐利地向上托起，记住 raise 是举起、提高。

root: 古诺斯语 reisa（举起、立起）→ 中古英语 raise → 现代英语 raise；与 rise、arise 同族。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an upward lift; the senses divide into lifting an object, raising a number, collecting money, bringing up the young, putting a subject forward and causing a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向上托举」；义项分为举起实物、提高数字、筹集钱款、养育幼小、提出话题与引起情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifted into the air, palm forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举到半空、掌心朝前的手。

branches.en: a box held above the head
branches.cn: 举过头顶的一只箱子

branches.en: a price tag rewritten higher
branches.cn: 被改写成更高数字的价签

branches.en: coins gathered from many hands
branches.cn: 从许多只手里聚拢的硬币

branches.en: a child guided step by step
branches.cn: 一步步被引导的孩子

branches.en: the same lift applied to a question and to a fear
branches.cn: 同一种抬升，一次用于问题，一次用于恐惧

intro.en: The word is a Norse borrowing, and English built its relatives with an agent suffix and a participle rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是古诺斯语借词，英语用施动者词尾与分词来构成亲属词，而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 受欢迎的；大众的；通俗的；民众的；普遍的
definition_en: liked or approved by many people; made for ordinary people rather than specialists; of the people as a political source; and held by most people
core_image: 小店门口排起长队，路过的人不知道卖什么，也先跟着排上
scene: 放学后的面馆门口总有人排队，队伍拐过墙角，连附近上班的人也来凑热闹。 That noodle shop is popular with students because it is cheap and fast.
sceneCN: 这里 popular 指「受欢迎的」（第 1 个义项：被很多人喜欢）；句意为这家面馆便宜又上得快，很受学生欢迎。图中可辨识场景：排到墙角的长队、放学的学生、探头张望的路人。

pos.zh: 受欢迎的；大众的；通俗的；民众的；普遍的

derivatives.zh: 由 popular 加 -ity 构成，义为「受欢迎；人气」
由 popular 加 -ize 构成，义为「使普及；使通俗化」
由 popular 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；由民众」
由 popular 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不受欢迎的」

senses.title: Liked by many people
senses.definition: liked, approved of or supported by a large number of people
senses.definitionCN: 被很多人喜欢、认可或支持的
senses.example: The new teacher quickly became popular with her class.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的老师很快就受到班上学生的欢迎。
senses.why: Latin popularis meant belonging to the people; a thing that belongs to everybody is one everybody is ready to accept, so approval grows out of that shared ownership.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 popularis 意为属于民众的；一样东西既然属于所有人，大家就都愿意接受它，「受欢迎」正是从这种共有关系里长出来的。

senses.title: Made for ordinary people
senses.definition: designed for ordinary people rather than for experts, and therefore easy to follow
senses.definitionCN: 面向普通人而非专家，因而容易听懂的
senses.example: He writes popular books about astronomy for readers with no training.
senses.exampleCN: 他写的天文读物面向没有受过专业训练的读者。
senses.why: If something is of the people, it is also for the people, so the word came to mark work that avoids the language of specialists.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西属于民众，自然也是做给民众的，于是这个词用来标记那些避开专家术语的作品。

senses.title: Of the people as a political source
senses.definition: relating to ordinary citizens, especially as the source of political authority
senses.definitionCN: 与普通公民有关的，尤指权力来自他们的
senses.example: The constitution was approved by a popular vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这部宪法经民众投票获得通过。
senses.why: The oldest political sense keeps the Latin meaning almost untouched: authority rests with populus, the people, not with a ruler above them.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的政治义几乎原封不动保留了拉丁含义：权力属于 populus（民众），而不是属于高居于他们之上的统治者。

senses.title: Held by most people
senses.definition: believed or repeated by a large part of the public, whether or not it is true
senses.definitionCN: 被大部分公众相信或传说的，不论真假
senses.example: It is a popular belief that we only use ten percent of our brains.
senses.exampleCN: 人们普遍相信我们只用了大脑的百分之十。
senses.why: Once an idea belongs to the many, it counts as popular even when it is wrong, which is why the word can sit directly beside belief and misconception.
senses.whyCN: 一个说法一旦属于很多人，即使它是错的也被称作 popular，所以这个词能直接修饰「看法」和「误解」。

intro.en: Popular came from Latin through French with the plain sense of belonging to the people; only later did English add the warmer sense of being liked.
intro.cn: popular 经法语来自拉丁语，本义只是「属于民众的」；「受喜爱」这层更暖的意思是很晚才由英语添上的。

items.en: Populus was the body of citizens, the people seen as a single crowd.
items.cn: populus 指公民的整体，是把人们看作一群人。

items.en: Popularis meant belonging to, pleasing or favouring the people, and it could describe a politician who courted them.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的、讨民众喜欢的、站在民众一边的，也能形容讨好民众的政治人物。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as populaire, keeping both the neutral and the approving tones.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 populaire，中性义与赞许义都保留着。

items.en: Middle English populere meant common, of the common people, and could still carry a hint of vulgar.
items.cn: 中古英语的 populere 意为普通的、平民的，仍可能带一点「粗俗」的意味。

items.en: Modern English pushed the word towards approval and, in politics, towards the people as the source of authority.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义推向「受认可」，在政治语境里则推向「权力来自民众」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the populus family and its negated form; the near-meaning group gathers words for being widely known or widely held.
note.cn: 形近组收 populus 词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示广为人知、广为接受的词。

entries.definition: The state or degree of being liked by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的状态或程度。

entries.definition: To make something widely known, used or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知、广为使用或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: Full of people; having a large population.
entries.definitionCN: 人口众多的；人烟稠密的。

entries.definition: Not liked or approved of by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 不被大多数人喜欢的；不受欢迎的。

entries.definition: Known by a great many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被很多人知道的；著名的。

entries.definition: Found, done or believed by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 大多数人都有的、做的或相信的；常见的。

entries.definition: Existing or happening over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大范围或许多人中存在的；普遍的。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with a Latin noun for the people, and each modern sense measures some way in which a thing belongs to them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起于拉丁语里表示民众的名词，每个现代义项都在衡量某样东西以何种方式属于他们。

normal.en: Latin popularis meant of the people, and being liked is simply being accepted by the people who own it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 popularis 意为属于民众的，而「被喜欢」不过是被拥有它的那群人接受。

normal.en: Popular and population share populus: one counts approval, the other counts heads.
normal.cn: popular 与 population 共用 populus：一个数的是认可，一个数的是人头。

normal.en: Popularity is popular plus -ity, the state of being liked seen as a quantity.
normal.cn: popularity 是 popular 加 -ity，把「被喜欢」看成一种可计量的状态。

normal.en: Popularize is popular plus -ize, to make something common among people.
normal.cn: popularize 是 popular 加 -ize，让某样东西在人们中间变得普遍。

normal.en: Popular with names the crowd that likes it; popular for names the reason.
normal.cn: popular with 后面接喜欢它的人群；popular for 后面接喜欢它的原因。

abstract.en: A queue outside a small shop is popularity made visible.
abstract.cn: 小店门口的一条长队，就是看得见的人气。

abstract.en: What belongs to everyone ends up pleasing everyone, so ownership turns into affection.
abstract.cn: 属于所有人的东西，最后会让所有人喜欢，所有权就这样变成了好感。

abstract.en: A word can be popular and still be wrong, which is why belief takes the same adjective as music.
abstract.cn: 一个说法可以很流行又完全是错的，所以「看法」和音乐共用同一个形容词。

examples.en: This song is popular with children.
examples.cn: 这首歌很受孩子们欢迎。

examples.en: Popular science books explain hard ideas in plain words.
examples.cn: 科普读物用平实的语言解释难懂的概念。

examples.en: The mayor was elected by popular vote.
examples.cn: 市长是通过民众投票选出的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡普乐」——把知识泡进普通人的快乐里，大家就都喜欢；popular 就是受欢迎的、大众的。

root: 拉丁语 populus（民众）→ popularis（属于民众的）→ 古法语 populaire → 英语 popular；同族还有 population、populace。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is belonging to the people; it then splits into being liked, being made for them, coming from them politically, and being believed by them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「属于民众」；由此分出被他们喜欢、为他们而做、政治上来自他们，以及被他们相信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue curling round the corner of a small shop, strangers joining it without asking why.
core.cn: 核心意象：小店门口的长队拐过墙角，陌生人没问缘由也排了进去。

branches.en: a queue curling round the corner of a noodle shop
branches.cn: 绕着面馆墙角的长队

branches.en: a plain-language guide to the stars on a bestseller table
branches.cn: 畅销书台上那本讲星星的通俗读物

branches.en: a ballot box where each citizen counts once
branches.cn: 每位公民都只算一票的投票箱

branches.en: a saying repeated in every kitchen and every office
branches.cn: 每个厨房和办公室都在重复的一句老话

branches.en: a leader who is both liked and chosen
branches.cn: 既被喜欢又被选出来的领导人

intro.cn: 一个表示民众的拉丁名词及其形容词撑起这个词，英语后缀则各管一段：-ar 造形容词，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造表「使……」的动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.

definition_zh: 组；群；团体；集团；（动词）把……分组；归类
definition_en: a number of people or things that are placed or considered together; to put people or things into such a set
core_image: 几个人肩并肩围成一个圈：单独的人聚在一起就成了一个整体
scene: 英语课上新来的老师让大家自由组合完成项目，同学们很快各自围成了小圈子。 The students formed a group to work on the science project.
sceneCN: 这里 group 是「小组、团体」（第 1 个义项：因共同目的聚在一起的人）；句意是学生们组成小组来做科学项目。

derivatives.zh: 由 group 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「分组；归类」
由 re-（重新）+ group 构成，义为「重新集结；重组」

senses.title: A set of people together
senses.definition: several people who are together or connected in some way
senses.definitionCN: 因共同目的、关系或位置聚在一起的一些人
senses.example: A group of tourists gathered outside the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 一群游客聚集在博物馆外面。
senses.why: The core image is people standing shoulder to shoulder, so the human crowd sense grows straight out of the picture.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是人们肩并肩围在一起，所以「一群人」这个义项最贴近画面本身。

senses.title: A set of things of the same kind
senses.definition: several things that belong or are placed together
senses.definitionCN: 放在一起或属于同类的几样东西
senses.example: She put the keys in the group of small metal objects on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她把钥匙放进桌上那堆小金属物件里。
senses.why: When the image no longer needs people, any collection of similar items can fill the same circle shape.
senses.whyCN: 当画面里不再需要人时，任何同类物品都能填进同一个圈，于是延伸出「一组物品」。

senses.title: An organization or company
senses.definition: a number of companies or organizations controlled in a similar way
senses.definitionCN: 由同一家管理或控制的若干公司或组织
senses.example: The media group owns three newspapers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家传媒集团拥有三家报纸。
senses.why: A company made of many parts is itself a crowd of smaller units, so the crowd image extends to business.
senses.whyCN: 企业由许多小单位聚成，本质还是「聚成一团」，画面延伸到商业领域就成了「集团」。

senses.title: A category for sorting
senses.definition: a set into which things are divided for study or organization
senses.definitionCN: 为研究或整理而划分出的一类
senses.example: Divide the animals into groups by size.
senses.exampleCN: 按体型把这些动物分成几类。
senses.why: Drawing a circle around similar things is exactly how people classify, so the picture becomes a sorting tool.
senses.whyCN: 在同类东西外面画个圈，这正是分类的动作，画面自然变成了分类工具。

senses.title: To put into sets
senses.definition: to place people or things together because they share a feature
senses.definitionCN: 把有共同点的人或物聚在一起放置或整理
senses.example: The teacher grouped the pupils by reading level.
senses.exampleCN: 老师按阅读水平给学生分组。
senses.why: Once the circle exists as an idea, drawing it becomes an action, so the noun turns into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 「圈」这个概念一旦确立，画圈就成了动作，名词顺理成章转成动词。

intro.en: The word group entered English relatively late and carries the idea of a drawn cluster.
intro.cn: group 进入英语的时间相对较晚，一直保留着「聚成一团」的画面。

items.en: Italian gruppo meant a knot or cluster, used by artists for a cluster of figures in a painting.
items.cn: 意大利语 gruppo 指结块、一簇，画家用它指画中聚在一起的一组人物。

items.en: The Italian word itself is often traced to Germanic grondo related to the root of grunt, though this is disputed.
items.cn: 意大利语这个词一般认为可追溯到日耳曼语 grondo，与 grunt（咕哝）的词根有关，但此说存疑。

items.en: English borrowed gruppo as group around the late seventeenth century, first for clusters of figures in art.
items.cn: 约十七世纪末英语借入 gruppo，拼作 group，最初用于艺术作品中的人物群像。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the meaning widened to any collection of people or things.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，词义扩大到任何聚在一起的人或物。

items.en: Modern usage added the verb sense and the business sense of a group of companies.
items.cn: 现代用法又增加了动词义和「企业集团」义。

note.en: These words are close in form or meaning to group.
note.cn: 这些词在词形或词义上与 group 相近。

entries.definitionCN: 葡萄，成串长在藤上；与 group 只是拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: to feel about with the hands uncertainly
entries.definitionCN: 摸索；与 group 拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a large game bird; also to complain

entries.definition: a tight group of similar things growing or held together
entries.definitionCN: 一簇；一群，强调密集聚在一起

entries.definition: a large number of people gathered together

entries.definitionCN: 一伙；一队，常指为一事联合的人

normal.en: gr + oup: think of a group standing in a circle
normal.cn: gr + oup：想象一群人围成一圈，正是「组」的画面。

normal.cn: 葡萄在藤上成串聚生，grape 和 group 都来自聚集的画面。

normal.cn: in groups of four（四人一组）是课堂固定表达，背下来即会用。

normal.en: group work means working together, not alone
normal.cn: group work 即小组合作，词义和场景绑定记忆。

normal.en: the verb group things means to sort them into circles
normal.cn: 动词 group things 就是把东西「圈」进不同类别。

abstract.en: one circle drawn around many dots
abstract.cn: 在许多圆点外画一个圈，圈住的就是一个 group。

abstract.en: shoulders touching, one unit
abstract.cn: 肩并肩挤在一起，散点变成一个整体。

abstract.en: many hands, one task
abstract.cn: 许多只手做同一件事，就是团队。

examples.en: The class split into three groups for the quiz.
examples.cn: 全班为测验分成了三个小组。

examples.en: Group the cards by color before you start.
examples.cn: 开始前先把卡片按颜色分组。

examples.en: A small group of villagers repaired the bridge.
examples.cn: 一小群村民修好了那座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「孤扑」——一个人孤单地扑向人群，终于加入了一个 group（小组）。

root: 一般认为来自意大利语 gruppo（一簇、结块），可能进一步追溯到日耳曼语与 grunt（咕哝）相关的词根，此说存疑；核心画面是「聚成一团」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a crowd of people to any collection, then to organizations and sorting, and finally to the verb of drawing circles.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从「一群人」扩展到「一组物品」，再到「机构、类别」，最后发展出「分组」的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many units inside one circle
core.cn: 核心意象：许多单位被同一个圈圈住

branches.en: people gathered as one body
branches.cn: 聚为一体的一群人

branches.en: items that belong together
branches.cn: 归在一处的一组物品

branches.en: companies under one control
branches.cn: 同属一管的机构集团

branches.en: a class made for sorting

branches.cn: 画圈归组的动作

latinIntro.cn: 校园文本中常与 group 同现的拉丁语系近形词。

The grouping of the data took hours.

definition_zh: 建议；劝告；通知；提供咨询
definition_en: to tell someone what you think they should do, or to inform them formally
core_image: 老师俯身给学生指点下一步
scene: 老师俯下身，给学生的下一步学习提出建议。 The teacher advised him to read the chapter twice.
sceneCN: 这里 advised 是「建议」（第 1 个义项：告诉别人该怎么做）；句意为老师建议他把这一章读两遍。

pos.zh: 动词：建议；劝告；通知；提供咨询

derivatives.zh: 建议；忠告
顾问
咨询的

senses.title: To suggest what to do
senses.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人你认为他该怎么做
senses.example: The teacher advised us to read more.
senses.exampleCN: 老师建议我们多读书。
senses.why: Advise is the verb form of advice, so it names the act of giving someone a view.
senses.whyCN: advise 是 advice 的动词形式，指把看法给某人的动作。

senses.title: To warn against something
senses.definition: to tell someone not to do something
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人不要做某事
senses.example: I advise you not to go out in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 我劝你不要在暴风雨里外出。
senses.why: The same act with a warning in it becomes telling someone not to do something.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作带上警告，就变成劝某人不要做某事。

senses.title: To tell someone formally
senses.definition: to give someone information in an official way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式方式把消息告诉某人
senses.example: Please advise us of any change.
senses.exampleCN: 如有变动请通知我们。
senses.why: In offices and letters, the act of giving information is the formal sense of telling someone.
senses.whyCN: 在办公室与信件里，把消息给对方的动作就是正式通知。

intro.en: The recorded history of advise is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 advise 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Advisare meant to look at or to consider, from the verb to see.
items.cn: advisare 意为察看或考虑，来自表示看的动词。

items.en: Aviser meant to think about and to give an opinion.
items.cn: aviser 意为考虑并给出意见。

items.en: English borrowed advise for giving an opinion to someone.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪借入 advise，指向某人提出意见。

items.en: The noun advice and the verb advise took different endings.
items.cn: 名词 advice 与动词 advise 采用了不同词尾。

items.en: Today it also means informing someone in an official way.
items.cn: 今天它也指以正式方式告知某人。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The third person form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: The past form of the verb.
The noun for the opinion given.

entries.definition: It stresses telling someone about a risk.
entries.definitionCN: 强调提醒某人注意风险。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ad- means to and visere means to see: to advise is to show someone how to see a choice.
normal.cn: ad- 表示向，visere 表示看：advise 就是把如何看待选择指给别人。

normal.en: The same family also gives advice and adviser.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 advice 与 adviser。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase advise caution.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「劝人谨慎」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of advise in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 advise 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to tell someone what you think they should do, or to inform them formally.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「建议」时用它。

abstract.cn: 想象老师俯身给学生指点下一步。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of advise grows from one core image: a teacher leaning down to point a pupil toward the next step.
sensesIntro.cn: advise 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：老师俯身给学生指点下一步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher leaning down to point a pupil toward the next step
core.cn: 核心意象：老师俯身给学生指点下一步

branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：建议。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: To warn against something.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：劝告不要做。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: To tell someone formally.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：正式通知。

definition_zh: 直的；直接的；指挥；导演；对准；直率的
definition_en: straight; without anything in between; to guide or aim something
core_image: 一条不拐弯的直线，或一只手指向前方的手
scene: 体育课上，班长站在队首。 The teacher asked the captain to direct the class to the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 direct 是「指挥、带领」（第 2 个义项：引导方向）；句意是老师请体育委员把队伍带到操场去。

derivatives.zh: direct 加 -ion 构成，义为「方向；指示」
direct 加 -or 构成，义为「导演；主管」
direct 加 -ly 构成，义为「直接地」
同根词，义为「名录；电话簿」
加前缀 in-（不），义为「间接的」

senses.title: Straight, without bending or stopping
senses.definition: going straight from one place to another, or with nothing in between
senses.definitionCN: 从一处直达另一处，中间没有别的东西
senses.example: There is a direct bus from our school to the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 从我们学校到博物馆有一趟直达公交。
senses.why: The Latin root means arranged in a line, so the core image is an unbent line between two points.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「排成直线」，核心意象是两点之间一条不弯的线。

senses.title: To guide or lead
senses.definition: to tell people what to do, or to lead an activity
senses.definitionCN: 指示人们做什么，或主持一项活动
senses.example: The music teacher will direct the school choir this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年将由音乐老师指挥校合唱团。
senses.why: A straight line needs a starting hand, so making things go straight became leading them.
senses.whyCN: 直线需要一个起点，让事物走直线便变成了「引导」。

senses.title: To aim at a target
senses.definition: to point something at a person or place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物指向人或地方
senses.example: Please direct your eyes to the blackboard.
senses.exampleCN: 请把目光投向黑板。
senses.why: Aiming is choosing a straight path for a thing, so the line image grew into pointing.
senses.whyCN: 瞄准就是为某物选定一条直路，线的意象便长成了「指向」。

senses.title: Honest and straight in speech
senses.definition: saying what you mean plainly
senses.definitionCN: 直截了当地说出想法
senses.example: Be direct with me: did you break the window?
senses.exampleCN: 跟我说实话：窗户是你打碎的吗？
senses.why: Words that travel in a straight line touch the point fast, so honest speech is called direct.
senses.whyCN: 话走直线，很快点到要害，于是坦率的话语被称作 direct。

intro.en: Direct comes from Latin words about making straight.
intro.cn: direct 来自拉丁语中表示「拉直」的词。

items.en: Latin dirigere meant to lay straight or to arrange, built on di- (apart) plus regere (to make straight, to rule).
items.cn: 拉丁语 dirigere 意为使成直线、安排，由 di-（分开）加 regere（使直、统治）构成。

items.en: The past participle directus meant straight or straightened.
items.cn: 过去分词 directus 意为直的、被拉直的。

items.en: Regere also gave regent and rule in later languages.
items.cn: regere 后来还派生出 regent（摄政者）和 rule（统治）。

items.en: English borrowed direct via Old French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语经古法语借入 direct。

items.en: At first it described lines and roads, then commands and films came later.
items.cn: 最初形容直线与道路，指挥义与电影义出现得更晚。

items.en: Modern English keeps straight, lead, aim and honest senses together.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留直、领导、瞄准、坦率等义项。

note.en: These words share the regere root or the straight-line field.
note.cn: 这些词同出 regere 词根，或属于直线义场。

normal.cn: 上课时 be direct 指直接说出你的想法。

senses.title: An official document for travelling abroad
senses.definition: an official document issued by a government that identifies you and allows you to travel to other countries
senses.definitionCN: 由政府签发、证明身份并允许你前往他国旅行的官方证件
senses.example: My passport expires next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 我的护照明年春天到期。
senses.why: The word joins passing and a port: the paper that once let a traveller through a harbour gate became the paper that lets a person cross a border.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「通过」与「港口」拼在一起：最初让旅客通过港口关卡的文书，后来成了让人跨越国境的证件。

senses.title: A permit to pass through a place
senses.titleCN: 通行证；通过某地的许可
senses.definition: an official paper allowing a person or a ship to enter, leave or move through a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 准许某人或某船进出、通过某地的官方文书
senses.example: In the old harbour, no ship sailed without a passport from the governor.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的港口，没有总督签发的通行证，任何船都不能出海。
senses.why: Before modern borders existed, a passport was aimed at a gate or a harbour rather than at a country, and history books still use the word that way.
senses.whyCN: 在现代国界形成之前，passport 针对的是一道关口或一个港口，而不是整个国家，历史叙述里至今保留这层用法。

senses.title: A means of reaching something
senses.definition: something that makes it possible for you to go somewhere or to achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 使你得以进入某地或取得某种成就的东西
senses.example: A good command of English is a passport to better jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的英语能力是获得更好工作的敲门砖。
senses.why: If a passport opens a border, then any paper, skill or contact that opens a door can borrow the name, because the movement from document to opportunity is the same.
senses.whyCN: 既然护照能打开国界，那么任何能打开一道门的证书、技能或人脉都可以借用这个称呼，因为「从证件到机会」的这一步是相同的。

intro.en: Passport fuses a verb of stepping with the Latin word for a harbour, and the paper it names has kept that gate-opening picture for six centuries.
intro.cn: passport 把表示「迈步」的动词与拉丁语里的「港口」合在一起，这个证件名称也因此把「打开关口」的画面保留了六百多年。

items.en: Passus was a step or a pace, naming the ground a foot could cover in one stride.
items.cn: passus 意为一步、一步的距离，指一只脚迈一次所跨过的地面。

items.en: The verb passare grew from that noun and meant to step, to go through or to go by.
items.cn: 动词 passare 由这个名词发展而来，意为迈步、穿过、从旁经过。

items.en: Old French passer carried the verb into everyday speech, and a compound of passer with port named a paper for passing a port.
items.cn: 古法语 passer 把这个动词带入日常语言，passer 与 port 组成的复合词则指准许通过港口的文书。

items.en: Medieval Italian passaporto recorded the same compound for a document that let a ship or a person leave a port, and French passed the form on to English.
items.cn: 中古意大利语 passaporto 记录了同样的复合词，指让船只或人员离开港口的文书，法语又把这一形式传给了英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the travel document as the main sense and extends the word to anything that opens a way, from a skill to a good name.
items.cn: 现代英语以出入境证件为主要义项，并把词义扩展到任何能打开通路的东西，从一门技能到好名声。

normalIntro.en: The word is a small machine of two parts: a verb for stepping and a noun for a harbour, locked together into one paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两部分咬合成一台小机器：一个表示迈步的动词，一个表示港口的名词，合成同一张纸。

normal.en: Pass means to go by, and port means a harbour, so a passport is literally a paper for going through a port.
normal.cn: pass 意为经过，port 意为港口，所以 passport 字面上就是「通过港口的纸」。

normal.en: Airports still keep the old picture alive: passport control stands exactly where a gate would be.
normal.cn: 机场仍在延续这个旧画面：护照查验处就设在相当于关口的位置。

normal.en: The plural is regular, passports, because it is an ordinary countable noun.
normal.cn: 复数按规则加 s 写作 passports，因为它就是普通的可数名词。

normal.en: The phrase a passport to success shows how a document for borders turned into a word for opportunity.
normal.cn: a passport to success 这个说法显示出：一张管边界的证件如何变成了表示机会的词。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable, so the two parts are spoken as one word rather than as pass and port.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一个音节，因此两个部分读起来是一个词，而不是分开的 pass 与 port。

abstract.en: A passport is a state promising, in ink and paper, that you may be let through.
abstract.cn: 护照是国家用油墨和纸张作出的承诺：你可以被放行。

abstract.en: Every border turns a small book into a key, which is why the same word can later mean any key.
abstract.cn: 每一道国界都会把一本小册子变成钥匙，所以这个词后来能指任何一把钥匙。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that permission is a thing you can hold in your hand and lose in a minute.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒人：许可是可以握在手里、也能在一分钟内丢掉的东西。

examples.en: She showed her passport at the desk and was waved through.
examples.cn: 她在柜台出示护照，随即被示意通过。

examples.en: A second language can be a passport to work in another country.
examples.cn: 第二门语言可以成为到别国工作的途径。

examples.en: The old rule required every vessel to carry a passport from the port authority.
examples.cn: 旧时的规定要求每艘船都携带港务当局签发的通行证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死跑特」——出门在外最怕丢了它，还得赶紧跑；passport 就是护照。

root: 由古法语 passer（经过）与 port（港口）复合，源头可追到拉丁语 passus（一步）与 portus（港口）；本义是准许通过港口的文书。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a paper that opens a gate; the senses run from the travel document to the older harbour permit and then to any means of access.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一张能打开关口的纸；义项从出入境证件，到较早的港口通行许可，再到任何通往机会的途径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small dark booklet handed through a window in exchange for a nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本深色封面的小册子递进窗口，换来一次点头放行。

branches.en: a queue at a border desk in the early morning
branches.cn: 清晨边检柜台前的一条长队

branches.en: a ship waiting for a stamped paper before it sails
branches.cn: 一条等着盖章文书才敢出海的船

branches.en: a language certificate placed on a job application
branches.cn: 一份语言证书放在求职材料上

branches.en: the same paper serving a traveller and a vessel
branches.cn: 同一张纸先后服务于旅客与船只

branches.en: a gate that opens first for a ship and later for a career
branches.cn: 先是向船只、后是向职业打开的一道门

intro.en: Two Latin pieces hold the word together: a noun for a step with its verb, and a noun for a harbour that English still uses on its own.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分撑起这个词：一个表示脚步的名词及其动词，一个表示港口的名词，后者英语至今单独使用。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a paper allowing passage through a port
